The group had not needed to become a traditional celebrity spokesperson. Its music and its audience had created the value.This changed the possibilities for later artists. Hip-hop musicians would go on to develop relationships with sneaker companies, clothing labels, jewelry brands, and fashion houses. Those partnerships became a major part of the genre’s commercial ecosystem.Yet the deeper legacy of Run-DMC’s fashion influence was cultural. The group helped establish the idea that a rapper’s clothes could communicate affiliation, confidence, and regional identity. Streetwear was not separate from hip-hop. It was one of the ways hip-hop expressed itself.Raising Hell: The Album That Changed EverythingThe album’s impact was immediate. It became the first rap album to reach multiplatinum status, and it helped make hip-hop a major force in the broader music business. The group was no longer simply successful within rap. It was competing for the attention of mainstream rock and pop audiences.Rick Rubin, co-founder of Def Jam Recordings, played a key role in the album’s production. Rubin understood the power of stripped-down arrangements and the possibilities of bringing different musical worlds together. His work with Run-DMC emphasized the group’s natural strengths: rhythmic precision, forceful vocals, and a sound that could withstand the addition of rock guitar without losing its center.The album featured several of the group’s most enduring tracks, including “My Adidas,” “Peter Piper,” “It’s Tricky,” and “Walk This Way.” Each revealed a different side of the trio.“Peter Piper” showcased the interplay between Run and DMC, with their lines moving back and forth in a way that made the performance feel almost athletic. “It’s Tricky” combined a memorable hook with a tightly controlled rhythm, creating a record that was playful without sacrificing the group’s sharp delivery. “My Adidas” turned fashion into a statement of identity.The album’s greatest achievement was its balance. It did not rely entirely on one crossover hit or one production gimmick. The rock elements were part of a wider sound, and the group’s lyrical personality remained at the center.Raising Hell also arrived at a moment when the music industry was becoming more receptive to rap’s commercial possibilities. The album gave record companies a clear demonstration that hip-hop could sustain major sales and reach audiences across racial and geographic boundaries. It helped open doors for artists who followed, even though the opportunities were not distributed evenly.The album’s importance was later recognized by the Library of Congress, which selected it for preservation in the National Recording Registry. That recognition placed Raising Hell among recordings considered significant to American musical and cultural history.For Run-DMC, the album marked the point at which the group moved from influential pioneers to international stars. It also created a new challenge: how to follow a record that had changed the scale of their career.“Walk This Way”: The Wall Comes DownThe most famous moment on Raising Hell was the collaboration with Aerosmith on “Walk This Way.” The record became a landmark in the relationship between rap and rock, but its origins were more complicated than a simple meeting between two successful acts.Aerosmith’s original song had already supplied a memorable guitar riff and a rhythmic vocal performance. Hip-hop DJs had recognized its potential years earlier, using its opening passage as a breakbeat. Run-DMC were familiar with the music, and the idea of building a rap record around the riff was not entirely foreign to them.Rick Rubin proposed a more ambitious approach: instead of merely borrowing the instrumental passage, Run-DMC would remake the song and bring Aerosmith’s Steven Tyler and Joe Perry into the recording. The collaboration forced two musical worlds into direct contact.The resulting track was built around the original riff, but Run-DMC gave it a different energy. The guitars were hard and immediate, the drums were forceful, and the rappers delivered the verses with the confidence that had defined their earlier records. Tyler’s vocals and Perry’s guitar connected the new version to Aerosmith’s rock identity, while the trio retained control of the song’s rhythmic drive.The video made the concept impossible to miss. A wall separated the rock musicians from the rappers, and the performers eventually broke through it. The visual was simple, but it captured the cultural significance of the collaboration: two audiences that had often been kept apart were now sharing the same musical space.The song reached the Top 10 of the Billboard Hot 100 and became Run-DMC’s biggest crossover hit. MTV played the video heavily, helping the group reach viewers who might never have purchased a rap record before.The effect was not limited to sales. “Walk This Way” demonstrated that rap could coexist with rock without becoming a novelty or losing its identity. The record did not simply place a rapper over a rock instrumental. It created a collaboration in which both styles were essential.The success also helped revive Aerosmith’s commercial fortunes, illustrating that the exchange could benefit established rock artists as well as hip-hop performers. The song became a model for future collaborations, although later attempts to combine rap and rock would vary widely in artistic success.There is a tendency to describe “Walk This Way” as the moment hip-hop was invented for mainstream audiences. That overstates the case. Rap had been building audiences, releasing influential records, and breaking commercial barriers for years. Run-DMC themselves had already established a national profile.What the song did was accelerate the process. It brought rap to a much larger audience, made the genre harder for major media outlets to ignore, and proved that a hip-hop act could command attention at the center of popular music.It also helped change the way the public understood musical boundaries. Rap was not a passing novelty that had to remain in a separate category. It was a creative force capable of transforming the music that surrounded it.The success of Raising Hell changed the scale of what a rap career could look like. Run-DMC became one of the first hip-hop acts to enjoy the kind of commercial visibility traditionally associated with major rock bands and pop stars.They appeared in major magazines, performed on high-profile television programs, and toured to audiences that extended far beyond the neighborhoods where the music had originated. They became recognizable to people who did not necessarily follow hip-hop closely, and their clothes and music helped define the decade’s visual image of rap.Their success also mattered for the album format. Run-DMC helped establish that rap artists could sell millions of albums rather than relying primarily on singles and local popularity. That distinction influenced how record companies evaluated new acts and how artists planned their careers.The group was among the first rap acts to appear on the cover of Rolling Stone, a sign that the genre was beginning to receive recognition from publications that had historically focused on rock. They also helped bring rap onto major television stages and into the wider national conversation about popular music.But mainstream recognition came with complications. The more successful hip-hop became, the more record companies sought to identify which styles were most commercially attractive. Some artists found themselves pressured to make music that matched the expectations of executives, radio programmers, or television networks.Run-DMC’s own success demonstrated that an act could reach a large audience without abandoning its original character. The group had not become successful by dressing like a rock band or replacing its rhythmic approach with conventional pop songwriting. It had brought its own sound into the mainstream.That example was particularly important for artists who followed. A new generation of rappers could see that distinctive voices, regional identities, and uncompromising production choices could become commercial strengths rather than obstacles.Touring With the Beastie Boys: Hip-Hop on a Bigger StageRun-DMC’s tours helped expand the audience for rap and establish a model for live hip-hop performance. Their shows demonstrated that a group built around two MCs and a DJ could command the stage without a traditional rock-band lineup.The Beastie Boys became important partners in this process. As a young rap group with punk roots and an irreverent performance style, they complemented Run-DMC’s hard-edged sound while appealing to some of the same rock audiences.Touring together helped bring hip-hop into venues and communities where it had previously received limited exposure. It also created a shared performance environment in which different approaches to rap could coexist. Run-DMC’s disciplined, direct style contrasted with the Beastie Boys’ chaotic humor, showing audiences that hip-hop was not a single uniform sound.These tours also helped develop the economics of rap performance. Major tours required professional management, reliable production, marketing, and the ability to draw crowds across multiple cities. As hip-hop acts demonstrated that they could do those things, the industry’s assumptions about rap changed.The live show remained central to Run-DMC’s identity. Their records were powerful, but their performances gave fans a direct experience of the chemistry between Run and DMC and the skill of Jam Master Jay. The DJ was not a background accessory; he was an active performer whose timing and turntable work helped drive the music.Run-DMC helped show that hip-hop could fill large venues while retaining the call-and-response traditions and rhythmic energy of smaller parties. That lesson would become essential as rap tours grew into major commercial events.The Difficult Follow-Up: Tougher Than LeatherAfter the extraordinary success of Raising Hell, Run-DMC faced the problem every major act encounters after a career-defining release: how to move forward without repeating the same record.The group’s fourth album, Tougher Than Leather, arrived in 1988. It included tracks such as “Run’s House” and “Beats to the Rhyme,” which maintained the trio’s hard-edged production and competitive delivery. The album demonstrated that Run-DMC could still produce strong music, but its commercial impact did not match the phenomenon of Raising Hell.The release also accompanied a film of the same name, an attempt to extend the group’s identity into cinema. The movie’s disappointing reception became a distraction from the music, and the larger entertainment industry continued to look for ways to turn successful recording artists into multimedia properties.The period also brought wider changes in hip-hop. New artists were emerging with different production techniques, increasingly intricate lyricism, and more varied regional identities. Public Enemy were expanding the possibilities of political rap, while groups such as De La Soul and A Tribe Called Quest were developing alternative sounds. Gangsta rap was gaining visibility, and a younger generation of MCs was pushing the music in new directions.Run-DMC remained influential, but it was no longer the only group defining what rap could become. The genre they had helped reshape was now too large and diverse for any single act to control.That was both a sign of their success and a challenge to their position. Run-DMC had helped create the conditions for hip-hop’s expansion, and the expanding scene was producing artists who would not necessarily follow the same template.The group’s later work therefore belongs to a different stage of its story. Its role was no longer simply to introduce rap to new audiences. It had to find a place in a culture that was growing more complex, competitive, and musically diverse.Back from Hell: Searching for a New DirectionReleased in 1990, Back from Hell reflected a group navigating a changing musical landscape. Hip-hop was moving rapidly, and the production styles that had once made Run-DMC sound startlingly new were becoming part of the genre’s vocabulary. New York rap was expanding in several directions, while West Coast artists were developing increasingly prominent regional sounds.The album contained tracks such as “Pause” and “What’s It All About,” but it did not restore the trio to the commercial position it had enjoyed in 1986. The music industry was also changing. Labels wanted new stars, audiences were developing different tastes, and hip-hop’s growth meant that even pioneering artists had to compete for attention.Run and DMC also experienced personal changes during this period. Run’s religious beliefs became increasingly important to him, and he eventually became an ordained minister. The members began exploring paths beyond the group’s original identity, although they continued to perform and record together.It would be misleading to treat the period as evidence that Run-DMC had become irrelevant. Their influence was already embedded in the music. The harder, sample-based approach that they had helped popularize was now a foundation for a much wider movement. Their position had changed partly because the genre had grown beyond the boundaries of the scene they helped bring into the mainstream.Down with the King: A Return to FormThe title track became a successful single and introduced the trio to listeners who had grown up with a newer generation of rap artists. The album featured production contributions from people associated with the evolving East Coast scene, including Pete Rock and Q-Tip, placing Run-DMC in conversation with artists who had developed under the influence of the group’s earlier work.That connection was meaningful. The group was no longer simply the act that had broken rap into the mainstream. It was now a respected elder presence whose sound and history had helped shape the artists leading the next phase of hip-hop.Down with the King also demonstrated that Run-DMC could adapt without completely abandoning its musical principles. The group still relied on forceful delivery, rhythmic interplay, and direct production, but the album reflected the more layered, sample-rich sound that had become prominent in early-’90s rap.The record was a commercial and critical improvement over the group’s previous releases, although it did not recreate the extraordinary crossover success of Raising Hell. By then, hip-hop had expanded into multiple regional scenes and stylistic movements. Run-DMC remained important, but the center of attention had shifted.The album’s legacy lies partly in the way it connected generations. It offered evidence that the group’s importance was not confined to the 1980s. Its members could still participate in a changing culture, work with younger producers, and make music that belonged to the present rather than existing only as a tribute to the past.Jam Master Jay: The Essential Third MemberRun-DMC’s history cannot be told accurately as a story about two rappers with a DJ standing behind them. Jason Mizell, known as Jam Master Jay, was a vital part of the group’s identity and success.Jay’s turntable work helped create the sound that connected the two MCs. His timing, scratches, record choices, and musical instincts gave the group a rhythmic foundation. Onstage, he helped maintain the energy of the performance and reinforced the relationship between hip-hop’s DJ tradition and its emerging album-oriented culture.His importance extended beyond technical skill. Jay was an integral member of the group, and his presence helped balance the personalities of Run and DMC. The trio’s chemistry was built around three distinct roles, and removing any one of them would have changed the sound and character of Run-DMC.Jay also remained connected to Queens as the group’s career evolved. He worked with younger artists and helped develop new talent through his own recording and production activities. His studio became a place where emerging musicians could work, and his influence extended into a new generation of New York rap.That work made his death especially devastating to the hip-hop community.On October 30, 2002, Jay was shot and killed at a recording studio in Queens. His murder shocked fans, fellow musicians, friends, and family members. The killing remained unresolved for many years, and the legal proceedings that followed brought renewed attention to the case. The loss was not only the death of a celebrated performer; it was the loss of a musician and community figure whose contributions to hip-hop had been fundamental.Jay’s death also changed the way many people understood Run-DMC’s history. The group’s public image had always emphasized unity, and its three-member identity was central to its legacy. His absence made clear that the story of Run-DMC could not be reduced to its hits or its place in music-industry history. It was also the story of three people whose friendship, work, and shared experiences had created something lasting.Run-DMC’s Influence on the Next GenerationThe strongest evidence of Run-DMC’s importance is the number of later artists who built careers using ideas the group helped popularize.Their stripped-down production helped establish the viability of hard, drum-driven rap. Their vocal interplay demonstrated how two MCs could create excitement by trading lines, finishing each other’s phrases, and delivering sections in unison. Their fashion choices showed that a group could build a powerful visual identity from everyday streetwear. Their success on television and in major venues helped establish a commercial path for hip-hop artists who followed.The Beastie Boys, LL Cool J, Public Enemy, and countless other performers emerged in a landscape that Run-DMC had helped change. Later artists such as Jay-Z and Eminem also recognized the group’s importance to the genre’s development. Their influence can be heard in different ways across East Coast rap, alternative hip-hop, and the broader history of MC-driven music.Not every later artist copied Run-DMC’s sound, and that is precisely the point. Their greatest contribution was not creating a formula that everyone had to follow. It was proving that rap could be commercially successful while maintaining its own identity.Artists could experiment with jazz samples, funk loops, electronic sounds, complex rhyme patterns, political themes, or regional musical traditions because hip-hop had become a recognized force in popular music. Run-DMC helped expand the space in which those experiments could happen.Their influence also extended to the relationship between performers and audiences. The group’s clothes, gestures, and direct delivery created a connection that fans could reproduce in their own lives. Hip-hop became not only a form of music to listen to but also a culture to participate in.The Business Legacy: From Rap Records to Cultural BrandsRun-DMC helped change the commercial model for hip-hop artists.Before the group’s breakthrough, record companies often treated rap as a niche market or a trend whose lifespan was uncertain. Run-DMC’s success demonstrated that a group could sell albums in large numbers, tour nationally, build a distinctive image, and generate commercial opportunities outside the record itself.The Adidas partnership was an early landmark in that process. It showed that a hip-hop group could influence consumer behavior through its own cultural authority. The group was not simply paid to wear a brand; it had already helped make the sneakers meaningful to its audience.That model became increasingly important in later decades. Rappers would build businesses in clothing, footwear, beverages, media, and entertainment. Some would become major entrepreneurs, using their musical visibility to develop companies with global reach.Run-DMC did not create every element of this business model, but it helped demonstrate the commercial value of hip-hop’s cultural identity. It showed that an artist’s sound, clothing, language, and audience could work together as a coherent brand.There was a risk in this development, too. As hip-hop became more profitable, corporations increasingly sought to market the culture, sometimes emphasizing its most easily packaged elements. The relationship between artistic independence and commercial success would become a recurring issue throughout the genre’s history.Run-DMC’s own career illustrated both sides. Their distinctive identity helped them reach a huge audience, while the pressures of success, changing tastes, and the expectations of the entertainment industry made it difficult to sustain their position at the top indefinitely.Even so, the commercial opportunities they helped establish became part of the infrastructure of modern hip-hop.Recognition and the Rock & Roll Hall of FameIn 2009, Run-DMC was inducted into the Rock & Roll Hall of Fame. The recognition placed the group among the performers whose work had significantly shaped the development of popular music.The honor reflected several distinct achievements: the group’s influence on the sound of recorded rap, its commercial breakthroughs, its role in bringing hip-hop to MTV and major concert stages, and its ability to connect rap with rock without sacrificing its identity.The group’s later recognition also reflected a broader shift in how music history was being understood. Hip-hop had once been dismissed by some commentators as a passing fad or a commercial novelty. By the 2000s, its importance to American music was undeniable, and Run-DMC stood near the center of that transformation.The group also received a Grammy Lifetime Achievement Award in 2016, further recognizing its long-term influence. These honors did not create its legacy; they acknowledged one that had already been established through decades of music, performances, and influence on other artists.Awards are only one way to measure cultural importance, but in Run-DMC’s case, they reflect a larger change in the music industry. Rap had become central to popular culture, and the pioneers who helped establish its commercial footing were increasingly recognized as major figures in music history.Why Run-DMC Still MattersRun-DMC’s story is sometimes reduced to a handful of familiar images: Adidas sneakers, black hats, the Raising Hell cover, and the video for “Walk This Way.” Those images are memorable, but they only hint at the scale of the group’s contribution.The trio helped change the sound of rap by demonstrating the power of minimal, rhythm-centered production. It changed the presentation of rap by establishing a recognizable visual identity rooted in streetwear. It changed the business of rap by proving that hip-hop acts could sell albums at a major scale and attract corporate partnerships. And it changed the genre’s public standing by bringing rap into media and venues that had rarely given it prominent attention.The group also helped make hip-hop’s diversity possible. Rap did not remain frozen in the style of Run-D.M.C. or Raising Hell. The genre developed through political expression, jazz-based production, gangsta rap, alternative styles, regional movements, and increasingly complex approaches to lyricism. Run-DMC’s importance lies partly in helping create the conditions for that evolution.Their story also shows that influence and commercial dominance are not the same thing. The group eventually faced new competition, changing tastes, and personal challenges. It did not remain at the center of popular music throughout every stage of its career. But its influence continued even as other artists became more prominent.The three members each brought something essential. Run provided a commanding rhythmic style and a strong sense of performance. DMC brought a distinctive voice and lyrical presence. Jam Master Jay supplied the turntable skill and musical foundation that completed the group. Together, they built a sound and identity that could not be mistaken for anyone else’s.Their career was rooted in Queens, but its effects reached around the world. Young rappers learned from their records, fans copied their clothes, producers studied their arrangements, and the music industry adjusted its understanding of what rap could accomplish.Final Thoughts: Three Guys from Queens Who Changed the RulesRun-DMC did not invent hip-hop, and they were not the first artists to record rap, perform on television, or experiment with rock influences. Their achievement was different: they brought together musical innovation, a powerful visual identity, commercial ambition, and a direct connection to hip-hop culture at exactly the moment when the genre was ready to expand.“It’s Like That” and “Sucker M.C.’s” helped establish a new sound for recorded rap. Run-D.M.C. proved that a rap album could become a major commercial success. King of Rock challenged the boundaries between musical genres. Raising Hell brought hip-hop into the center of popular culture, and “Walk This Way” became a lasting example of what could happen when rap and rock met on equal terms.Their influence can still be seen in how rappers dress, how producers build beats, how MCs perform together, and how hip-hop artists approach the business opportunities surrounding their music.Most importantly, Run-DMC helped make it possible for rap to be taken seriously without having to sound like anything other than rap. They did not need to abandon their neighborhood identity, soften their delivery, or disguise their influences to reach a mass audience. They brought their own culture to the world and helped change what the world listened to.Three young men from Hollis, Queens, entered the music industry at a time when rap’s future was far from guaranteed. They left behind a legacy that reaches across generations and musical styles. Their records remain recognizable, their image remains iconic, and their contribution to hip-hop’s rise is woven into the history of modern music.Run-DMC changed the rules, and the artists who came afterward inherited a much larger playing field because of it.

item.title: Meet Prometheus, a Gift Link Search Engine
item.author: Jason Kottke
item.content:encoded: Sometime in the past few years, media sites like Bloomberg, The Economist, The Atlantic, Defector, Talking Points Memo, and the NY Times started offering a way for subscribers to share paywalled articles with friends and followers. These are commonly referred to as gift links.Thousands of gift links are shared on websites and social media daily. Some helpful aggregated feeds and hashtags are available, but finding specific information can be difficult. Whenever possible here on KDO, I link to paywalled articles with gift links. To help in that endeavor, I’ve built a gift link discovery tool called Prometheus.Prometheus collects gift links to paywalled news articles shared by subscribers — from the New York Times, the Washington Post, the Atlantic, and more. Links are gathered from Bluesky, Mastodon, and the web throughout the day, and you can search by keyword & URL and filter by publication.Right now, Prometheus is only available to active kottke.org members while I’m testing and refining it — it’s definitely a beta tool rn. If you’re a member, check it out and let me know if you’ve got any feedback or notice any rough edges.An informed public is the foundation of a healthy society — and while paywalls aren’t the only challenge here, they also aren’t helping. Big thanks to everyone sharing their gift links online and to these media companies for enabling their subscribers to share their journalism with others.

item.title: Panic in the Final Stretch
item.author: Josh Marshall
item.source: Josh Marshall – TPM – Talking Points Memo
item.content:encoded: One interesting dimension of the “Wedgewood Polls” story I discussed last night is that Republican leaders are latching on to it as evidence that all the polls are fake or at least wrong. Normally you might see this as part of election denial or setting the stage for questioning results. Maybe it’s some of that. But this looks much more like trying to prevent the bottom from falling out in an already bad situation. If your core partisans think the election is already lost a chunk of them just won’t show up to vote at all. And that’s how you can take a bad election night and turn it into a disaster.

item.content:encoded: Election rules vary state to state. Votebeat helps voters make sense of them. ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ Voting and elections have a lot of specific rules and regulations that — because U.S. elections are very decentralized — can change based on where you live. Rules that vary across the country include: the dates and times early voting may be available, whether no-excuse absentee voting is an option, and requirements for voter ID on Election Day. Elections are locally run and so various state laws determine a lot about how and when voters are able to vote. That’s why Votebeat is primarily local. We have five reporters embedded in key states across the country: Arizona, Michigan, Pennsylvania, Texas, and Wisconsin. My colleagues are specialized in knowing exactly how elections are run where they live — and they are the first to tell you if any of these rules have changed or are creating hurdles for voters at the polls.

The 2026 Squishing of the Squash
item.author: Miss Cellania
item.content:encoded: Since 1999, when a prize-winning 828 pound pumpkin was donated to the Oregon Zoo, the annual Squishing of the Squash has been a premiere event. Local farmers donate excess produce, and the elephants love it. For them, it's a combination of a ball game, a treasure hunt, and snack time. The crowds of humans love it, too. This year, the star of the show was an 18-year-old Asian elephant named Samudra. She was offered a 500 pound pumpkin that was stuffed with apples, sweet potatoes, and lettuce. She had fun playing with the gourd until it cracked open, revealing the surprise banquet. This will be the last Squishing of the Squash in Oregon for Samudra, as she is moving to the St. Louis Zoo next year. Her little sister Tula-Tu, only 20 months old, got her own smaller pumpkin. (via Laughing Squid)

item.title: Today's PHP Security Release, and How We're Strengthening PHP Security
item.author: Simon Willison
item.content:encoded: If you're running anything on PHP it's vital you upgrade - today's updates (across the entire PHP 8.x line) address two remote code execution holes, and there have been exploits circulating since last night, thanks to a leak in the coordinated disclosure process.This post from the PHP Foundation explain what went so wrong:On Tuesday, October 20th, at around 15:00 UTC, the two CVE IDs began circulating on online forums and social media. They came with a wrong release time and a wrong CVSS score of 10.0 (the actual score is 9.2). No technical details leaked. In response, the PHP project brought its pre-announcement forward and published it at 19:30 UTC. It also moved the release from October 22nd, 14:00 UTC, to October 21st, 14:00 UTC [...]As a result of the leak and pre-announcement around 20:00 UTC, Calif, one of the security firms that had reported the issues mistakenly published a video. It showed their proof of concept working against a number of targets and revealed a few additional, though limited, details about the vulnerabilities. Copies of the deleted video started circulating on social media soon after. The video contributed to accelerated development of various PoCs (exploitation proof of concepts), which then increased circulation on October 21st.This article from the team that discovered the original vulnerability includes a more detailed timeline of the original intended responsible disclosure: Wiz Research discovers the first PHP vulnerability using Wiz Atlas, Gemini 4 Argon, and GPT-5.6 Sol. Unauthenticated RCE is confirmed against Drupal. Unauthenticated RCE is confirmed against WordPress. Wiz Research reports the vulnerabilities to the PHP security team. PHP acknowledges the reports and begins developing a coordinated fix. Patched PHP releases become available. Public disclosure.

item.title: Robert Saleh Says Jordan Elliott Needs Help, Not Condemnation
item.author: Barry Petchesky
item.content:encoded: Tennessee Titans defensive tackle Jordan Elliott was a surprise inactive for Sunday's game, not traveling with the team. Head coach Robert Saleh told reporters only that Elliott was "dealing with personal stuff." On Tuesday, the Titans released Elliott, along with a cryptic statement referencing an "incident." One never wants to have an incident, but the lack of detail only made the whole thing more mysterious.Elliott and offensive tackle JC Latham got into a fight during drills at the Titans' facility, the reports say, and Elliott was told by coaches to leave the field. He left the building, going out to the players' parking lot with the intention of retrieving a gun from his car. Defensive lineman John Franklin-Myers, a real hero here, was able to talk Elliott out of getting the gun, and he never brought it back into the building.

item.title: ‘Digger’ Is Smug, Cynical, And Perfectly Timed
item.author: Osita Nwanevu
item.content:encoded: On the night of May 10, 1968, the most storied night in the last century of French civil unrest, nearly 40,000 students faced off against policemen in the Latin Quarter of Paris—one of the largest crowds the city's swelling protest movement had yet assembled. Famously, cobblestones were torn up from the streets to erect barricades. By the time morning broke, hundreds of demonstrators had been beaten bloody or arrested anyway. That same evening, the Cannes Film Festival opened with a ceremony hosted by retired actress Grace Kelly, Princess of Monaco, and a screening of a restored edition of .That juxtaposition quickly led to calls for the festival’s suspension. On May 18, after a week of resistance from Cannes’s organizers, a group of filmmakers and guests led by the directors Francois Truffaut and Jean-Luc Godard held a press conference demanding a closure. “There isn’t one film showing the problems going on today among workers and students⁠—not one, whether by Forman, myself, Polanski, or Francois,” Godard said. “There are none. We’re behind the times. Our student comrades set an example by getting their heads bashed in last week.” There were grumbles in the crowd at this, and Godard’s patience snapped. “We’re talking solidarity with students and workers, and you’re talking dolly shots and close-ups!” he yelled. “You’re assholes!”

item.title: How Much Fire Emblem Is Too Much Fire Emblem?
item.author: Luis Paez-Pumar
item.content:encoded: When I was on the fence about buying a Nintendo Switch 2, I held off with the self-aware knowledge that I would eventually cave come September. I knew that Fire Emblem: Fortune's Weave would break me. I needed to play this game like my life depended on it. https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=kmF38S_0vPs A month (and a few days) after release, I have 70-plus hours played on , and I wish it were double the amount. Still, 70 hours is a huge amount; aside from , I simply don't spend 70 hours on a single video game anymore. (The last "long" game I played was another strategy role-playing game, but even the remake only took me 36 hours to complete.) Fire Emblem is different, though. More than perhaps any video game series I have devoted chunks of my life to, Fire Emblem finds its way into both my waking thoughts and my sleeping nightmares. I began to see spreadsheets in the dark, thinking about ways to best build my virtual army of adorable murderers. I sought out the magic lightning Levin Swords in my deepest fantasies; words like "troubadour" and maybe-not-words like "bardinger" took on new meaning. I became obsessed, as fellow Defectorite Kathryn Xu could prove by producing even a portion of the many messages I have sent her about this game in just over a month.

item.title: DOJ’s List of Noncitizen Voters Exposed As Crap
item.author: David Kurtz
item.content:encoded: The top election official in Los Angeles County has done a preliminary review of the Trump DOJ’s purported list of alleged noncitizen voters and found it to be … shoddy. Surprising absolutely no one.Out of DOJ’s list of 20,000 alleged noncitizen voters in California, more than 7,000 had Los Angeles County addresses. Dean C. Logan’s office took a sample of 200 of those L.A. voters and found that 1/4 may have been born in the United States, nearly 1/2 were cancelled or inactive voters, and nearly 3/4 had never voted, according to a new court filing:It’s critically important to frame this properly: Election administrators must always balance making sure ineligible voters don’t vote with assuring that eligible voters aren’t wrongfully denied their right to vote. Make voting rules and regulations too strict and the risk goes up of excluding legitimate voters and not counting their votes.It’s a balance that Trump and Republicans refuse to strike in their jihad to vilify noncitizen voters and elevate a vanishingly small problem into a reason to distrust election results. It’s telling that they voice more apparent concern about what they call “vote dilution” by noncitizen voting than they do about outright denying U.S. citizens the right to vote and have their vote counted.In the California case, the shoddy list makes even more stark the incredible demand the Trump administration is suing to impose on the state. It wants California — with voting already underway — to introduce new additional steps into the vote tabulation process: review DOJ’s crap list, segregate all the ballots cast by people on that list, and run a real-time review to confirm whether those voters are citizens. Then — and only then — can California count those ballots.Note on whom the burden falls here: The Trump administration can supply a flawed and unreliable list, then California — while already conducting a live election — has to run around and jump through the extra hoops that the administration has created for it.Here’s how a top Los Angeles County election official put it in her own declaration in the case:Because the County results must be submitted by December 3, 2026, and certified by the State by December 11, 2026, ballots held pending an open-ended federal review may, in practical effect, never be counted. This process would risk disenfranchising voters who are validly registered. The process the DOJ seeks to have the Registrar undertake jeopardizes that core right for potentially thousands of voters, not to mention the finalization of election results, confidence in election results, and the ability to allow new elected officials to be instated in their positions.I should mention that the administration has offered to “help” California and work together in cooperative fashion to vet the administration’s crappy list, but it’s too precious an offer to need its own debunking:“We’re not perfect and that’s why we’ve asked California to cooperate with us,” acting Deputy Attorney General Trent McCotter said in a Monday press conference, anticipating exactly what happened yesterday. “These are the ones where we’re kind of the most confident that they are noncitizens.”“Kind of the most confident.”Dems Sue Trump for Election InterferenceVarious Democratic entities filed a new federal lawsuit in D.C. to try to block the worst of President Trump’s attacks on the midterm elections, including his demands to purge voter rolls and not count ballots, his threats against election officials, and his interference in state-run elections:The Corruption: $50M Woman EditionWhere to even start with this?The recently remarried Alina Habba, who now goes by Alina Mildon, landed a guaranteed $50 million deal to serve as general counsel of a brand new corporate entity tied to Venezuelan billionaire Julio Herrera Velutini, the NYT reports. Among the lowlights:The company — Concord Partners, LLC — was formed in Florida on Oct. 22, 2025 by Isabela Herrera, 27, the billionaire’s daughter and a U.S citizen.The deal was for $10 million a year for four years, plus bonuses, bringing the total guaranteed compensation to $50 million.Mildon “finalized the deal” while she was still the acting U.S. attorney in New Jersey.Mildon’s start date was Jan. 1, 2026. By then, Mildon was a senior adviser to then-Attorney General Pam Bondi, the role she took after being disqualified as U.S. attorney in New Jersey.President Trump pardoned Julio Herrera Velutini on Jan. 15, 2026.Mildon denies having any role in the pardon.The timing of this revelation may be connected to the epic ongoing feud between Mildon and Ric Grenell that has produced a sleazefest of competing allegations of off-the-charts corruption.Russia’s Failed Attack on GermanyThis still hasn’t broken through in the U.S., but over the summer, Russia intelligence launched a drone attack on a cargo plane carrying military assistance to Ukraine while it was parked at an airport in eastern Germany. It was the most dramatic of Putin’s provocations against NATO countries which have been on an uptick since that failed attack.The attack was part of a broader effort to position agents, explosives and weapons across Europe to strike targets supporting Ukraine and sow chaos that could strengthen political opposition to military aid for Kyiv, according to investigators and intelligence officials.Investigators have uncovered networks smuggling explosives, drones and weapons into the EU, along with safe houses and concealed underground caches near airports, arms manufacturers and other potential targets.There’s been a lot of chatter lately about whether World War III is already underway. I think that’s overdetermined, but it’s also true that we probably won’t notice until we’re deep into it.The Independent’s Andrew Feinberg writes about being targeted by President Trump as a “Mongoloid Moron” in the Oval Office yesterday — an outburst that the White House happily touted on social media.Who Gets to Define We the People?Jamelle Bouie: “[T]he drive to denaturalize Omar is, by itself, a startling attack on the liberty of all Americans. It’s a move that harks back to the worst of the nation’s past — those moments when the government sought to shape, define and ultimately choose who would be ‘the people’ of the United States.”In the racist rants of President Trump and his enablers, Somali Americans are both primitives who eat your pets and ingrates who are undeservedly “living the high life” at your expense:The only consistency is the rancid appeal to every base human emotion.

item.title: How The Rams Being 2-4 Relates To The Troy Aikman Saga
item.author: Drew Magary
item.content:encoded: In case you didn’t read about it, or you didn’t hear the hints firsthand, Joe Buck and Troy Aikman are reportedly getting divorced. The broadcast team is the longest-tenured booth duo in NFL history, even moving together from Fox to ESPN as a package deal four years ago. But Buck re-upped with the four-letter for a mint earlier this year, while Aikman, whose contract expires at the end of this season, was left to dangle. This perhaps represented the first time in history that Aikman did not say, “I completely agree with you, Joe,” to his longtime colleague. In fact, the men reportedly almost came to blows over Buck’s supposed betrayal. JUICY!Believe those reports if you like (I do), but either way, Aikman has already openly talked about his “next landing spot,” which means there’s gonna be a big fat vacancy in the booth for ESPN to fill come this spring. What does that have to do with the Rams being the biggest disappointment in football? THAT, dear friends, is one of the Big Questions that Arif Hasan and I tackle on this week’s episode of https://art19.com/shows/the-distraction/episodes/4484213c-a363-48a6-8228-1a6454eaa898

item.title: JD Vance is America’s worst insult comedian
item.content:encoded: Theories abound as to why JD Vance, once a promising Yale Law graduate with a best-selling memoir, went MAGA. Some argue that it was always a mistake to confuse the vice president’s cosmopolitanism for intellectual sophistication, pointing out that “Hillbilly Elegy” is a bad book that panders to ugly right-wing stereotypes about his working class family of origin. Others suggest he is an empty shell who will become whatever it takes to gain money and power, as evidenced by his constantly shifting attitudes about race and religion. The truth likely falls in the “why not both?” arena. After all, empty and insecure people have often been drawn to far-right ideologies. But there is one under-appreciated possibility for the MAGA turn of a man who once called Donald Trump “America’s Hitler”: that he finally found an audience willing to laugh at his unfunny jokes.Vance is clearly embroiled in a lifelong struggle with a common ailment of self-serious men who consider themselves profound geniuses. He longs to be the funniest guy in the room, but he is unable to understand how humor works. But the vice president has discovered what second-rate talents that end up as the “comic” relief on Fox News learned long ago: The right-wing crowd doesn’t care if you’re not funny just as long as you’re cruel. Vance is taking full advantage of MAGA’s lack of discernment in the last weeks of the midterm campaign. During a stop in Texas supporting the Republican Senate candidate, state Attorney General Ken Paxton, Vance responded to a fan by saying, “I love you, too, sir. And in a totally platonic way, to be clear. I’m the vice president, not James Talarico.” The audience roared with laughter, apparently unable to realize that calling Paxton’s Democratic opponent “gay” is less witty than if Vance had made fart noises with his armpit. The vice president can’t stop with tedious jokes about Talarico, who is leading in statewide polls. On his way to Texas, Vance falsely accused Talarico of having “a weird focus on transgender kids and drag queens,” topics that he and Trump bring up every chance they get. Vance added, “typically people who say stuff like that tend to have some pretty unusual search histories.” But Vance isn’t content to simply dabble in homophobia and transphobia. Racism is also his forte. During a North Carolina rally on Monday, he called non-white congresswomen “crazies” and mispronounced the name of Rep. Ilhan Omar, D-Minn. When a protester jumped up to demand that the Trump administration release the Epstein files, Vance suggested, apparently taking note of the young man’s darker skin, that the protester was in the U.S. because of “illegal border crossings.” At another event, Vance called Dr. Abdul El-Sayed, Michigan’s Democratic candidate for Senate, a “little weasel” who should “shut his mouth and show a little gratitude.” This was not out of character; the vice president often demands that people of color bow and scrape before white people for graciously allowing them to exist. But this time he got rebuked by the far funnier El-Sayed, who responded that Vance “had a cute little rally” with the “five people who like him.”But the vice president’s lack of wit was perhaps best illustrated at an Ohio rally in support of GOP gubernatorial candidate Vivek Ramaswamy, when he suggested that Dr. Amy Acton, the Democratic nominee, has a substance abuse problem. “Vance’s implication can be traced to a Republican ad that paints Acton as an alcoholic after a 2019 incident in which the police were called during a loud fight with her husband. The call was reported not violent by officers, and her campaign claims the situation is being blown out of proportion. (Acton has also been hit with ads featuring insults from her mother, Donna Arthur, with whom she has been estranged since 1978 after Arthur refused to support her when she accused her stepfather of molesting and raping her between the ages of nine and 12. According to the New York Times, Acton’s stepfather entered a not-guilty plea and was indicted by a grand jury, then went on the run from Ohio before standing trial.) Vance’s stream of insults ring particularly noxious when considering that he spent the summer portraying himself as a heartfelt Catholic convert whose salvation has imbued him with a newfound sense of Christian grace.Vance’s stream of insults ring particularly noxious when considering that he spent the summer portraying himself as a heartfelt Catholic convert whose salvation has imbued him with a newfound sense of Christian grace. In an obvious effort to soft-launch a 2028 presidential campaign, the vice president published “Communion: Finding My Way Back to Faith” in June, and strived mightily to convince interviewers they were beholding a humble servant of Jesus Christ. Vance told USA Today that “my faith tells me to fight against” the blind pursuit of ambition and instead “focus on the good” and “make wise decisions and moral decisions.” In an excerpt published in the Wall Street Journal, he wrote that he’s learned “to love all parts of our Christian communion,” including those “who voted for me and those who didn’t.” He went on “The View” with this gentle Christian message, claiming regret over “boneheaded” insults in the past, such as when he described childless women as being “miserable,” “sociopathic” and “cat ladies. The hosts weren’t having it, though, pointing out that there is nothing of Christian communion in the administration’s attacks on Black people and immigrants, and leaving a visibly uncomfortable vice president to pretend not to know what they were talking about. Vance may be able to wriggle around his very un-Christian insults and falsehoods about Democratic politicians by calling politics a “dirty business,” as he did in the Wall Street Journal. But it’s impossible to square his claims of grace and salvation with the utter nastiness he unleashes on immigrants, most of whom are Christians themselves. He has yet to apologize for falsely accusing Haitian immigrants — most of whom are Catholic, like himself — of stealing people’s dogs and cats to eat them. Shortly after publishing “Communion,” Vance accused immigrants of making America “dirtier and poorer and less safe and less prosperous.” (This is also flat-out false, as immigration has been proven to boost the economy, and the country is objectively cleaner than it was decades ago, when a thick cloud of smog hung over many American cities.)Through it all, Vance seems to be hoping that the crowd that sees his “Christian charity” face isn’t the same one showing up to hoot at his lame “no homo” jokes about the devout Talarico. This behavior was on display during his recent CBS town hall event, where he tucked away the bad insult comedy and put on his choir boy mask. The dishonesty and hypocrisy reached stratospheric levels when audience members, including a Catholic nun, challenged Vance on his support for mass deportations and his racist lies about immigrants. “To the extent that my rhetoric has been imperfect here,” Vance said, “that’s on me.” Then he framed the administration’s widespread abuses as reasonable, even compassionate, restrictions on immigration. His comments came mere hours after he falsely blamed the riots in France on immigrants, posing on X that “liberals imported the third world into France and other countries” while “ignor[ing] fundamental questions of assimilation and compatibility.” No doubt Vance would deflect and deny if he were confronted on it, but there’s no way to interpret his words except as a claim that people of different backgrounds cannot live together without violence — a frequent insinuation of his that is never slowed by the fact that his own wife and children are Indian-American. This is ultimately why — despite the undeniable ugliness of Vance’s insults of Democrats, immigrants, queer people and single women — his humor rarely generates the outrage he’s clearly trolling for. Vance tends to come across as more of a pathetic striver than an effective bully. Verbal jabs work a lot better if the would-be roaster has a sense of self- confidence, or at least the ability to fake it. Whether he’s speaking of love or hate, Vance never really seems to be talking with any conviction at all, beyond the hope that whatever he’s saying will win him more power.

item.title: Leadership Dispatch: Co-lead strategically
item.author: bounces+68ummn4ex9s8h5qmdlgaohppxkqm7h9hgzo3@ckespa.joshdoody.com
item.content:encoded: This week's Leadership Dispatch is about co-leadership. Managing your relationship with co-leaders may be more nuanced than leading a group. Think strategically about your relationship with your co-leaders, and how you portray the leadership team to the team you are leading.Before you begin co-leading, you should decide whether there is a hierarchy or whether all leaders are co-equal. If you are the ultimate leader and they are leaders who are also part of your team, then lead your co-leaders as you would other team members.But if you are co-equal, meaning that you and your co-leaders will generally have equal say, then the approach changes slightly. You’ll need to operate in a more collaborative way and defer more frequently than you would if you were the only leader.You will find that you don’t have a strong opinion on many decisions. On those decisions, you should just defer to your co-leaders.Occasionally, you have a strong opinion on a decision, and that is the time to cash in on the social capital you’ve accumulated by being deferential most of the time. If you almost always defer to your co-leaders, then when you suddenly have a strong opinion and do not immediately defer, that will carry a lot of weight.You should ultimately portray your leadership team as a single unit so that your team perceives you and your co-leaders to be in lockstep, even if you are not.

item.title: Ambient Earth
item.author: Jason Kottke
item.content:encoded: Ambient Earth is a 7.5-hour, real-time, 4K, remastered video of the orbital view from the International Space Station. Seán Doran took almost 49,000 images from 27 time-lapse sequences captured from the ISS by astronaut Butch Wilmore, repaired, remastered, and interpolated them into this incredible video.Perspective is lost when the world speeds by. The scale and beauty of our home planet is truly appreciated when observed on an epic 7.5 hour journey from The International Space Station. This ambitious 4k compilation, crafted through months of meticulous restoration, invites you to slow down and experience Earth in real time just as astronauts do.The video is accompanied by ambient audio recorded on the station by Chris Hadfield. This would be great for a screensaver, but after poking around for a bit, it doesn’t seem like there’s a good way to set a YT video as a screensaver on MacOS (without downloading it or having it be a livestream).

item.content:encoded: Folks, you can say what you want about Preznit Fuckwit, but you can’t deny that the dude is a bottomless well of super-awesome ideas.Let’s threaten and alienate all our allies. Let’s throw Ukraine to the wolves, and give Putin everything he wants. Let’s bomb the shit out of Venezuelan fishermen.Let’s allow masked federal thugs to roam the streets of our cities, and look the other way when they gun down anyone they want. Let’s smash half the White House to rubble, and put up a vulgar, heavily-militarized Epstein Dance Hall in its place. Let’s clownfuck ourselves into an unwinnable war that ends up making everything unaffordable.Let’s encourage Americans to rat each other out for fun and profit.Wait, what was that last one? Americans should do what?“So today, I’m thrilled to announce the— Fraud Whistle— Blower Incentive— Program. Fraud— Whistle— Blower Incentive Program. Annnnnnd— mark those words. Independent journalists and every— body and all Americans will now be able to go to the— fraud dot gov and report cases of corruption and theft of taxpayer dollars in their communities ... if you turn somebody in and you find $1 billion, we’re giving a commission of 1%. That's a lot of money,”Really? We’re paying bounties on fraudsters now? Because I know a guy who sleep-farted his way through an entire trial, and then got convicted on 34 counts of fraud. He’s still walking the streets, and he’s still criming. Can I turn this narcoleptic fuckface in, and glom some reward?The Donnyverse doesn’t intend for this new whistleblower thingumbob to be used against — and certainly not against .“They came here from Somalia, they’re living here for a year or two, they say ‘I’m going to open up a fake daycare. I’ll tell Keith Ellison, I’ll tell Governor Walz, I’m taking care of 200 kids. Send me a check for thirty million dollars. What do they do? They buy Mercedes, they buy BMWs. They buy a mansion, they buy a nice house. All their kids fly first class all over the world. They are living the high life.”Wait, is that true? Let’s do a quick fact check: this isn’t happening. It’s a fever-swamp fairy tale cooked up by white supremacists. The reality is that every accusation Nosferatu just shat our of his undead mouth is actually being perpetrated right now by Preznit Fuckwit’s two felonious failsons — Cokey McSniffles, and the dumb one. A report released Thursday details how the family of President Donald Trump “pocketed more than $2.9 billion”—including “in cash and gifts from crypto ventures, legal settlements, a luxury jet from a foreign government, and corporate deals”—while Republican cuts to the Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program left millions of Americans without critical food aid.Can I turn them in? Pick a lane, racists — are these Somalis all on welfare, or are they all buying luxury items? Because — spoiler alert — it can’t be both.Folks, this is straight up Nazi bullshit — because you know who else used to pay people to rat out the undesirables in their midst, don’t you? Of course you do.“The Dutch Department,” as the Nazis called it, was also known as the “Colonne Henneicke,” after its leader, Wim Henneicke. He had been trafficking in stolen Jewish property until the Nazis began offering cash for Jewish prisoners.Workers were paid about 15 guilders a week, or $75 at today’s exchange rate, plus 7.50 guilders or $37.50 per captured Jew, van Liempt writes.Pretty weird how every atrocity this administration is committing right now, was first dreamed up by the Nazis, 90 years ago. What a bizarre set of coincidences, am I right?There was a time when arriving at our shores with five dollars in your pocket, and then going on to make a success of yourself was called ‘living the American dream.’ We celebrated such people, and wrote books and made movies about them.Okay, that’s probably not the best example, The American dream isn’t a thing any more. The oligarchy doesn’t want some nasty immigrant coming here and succeeding — and certainly not any non-white immigrant. They want to keep all that money for themselves. (They made an exception for the Space Nazi — because, as a white child of privilege, he was already one of them.)Sixty out of a hundred thousand is 0.06 percent — a rounding error away from zero.Fraud in Minnesota is almost nonexistent, and the culprits have already been rounded up and dealt with — but racist shit-kadoodles like Nosferatu McGoebbels want you to believe that every Somali is guilty of , and that the America people won’t be safe until every single one of them has been deported to who the fuck even cares, just get them out of Dear Leader’s sight.All this is by design. It’s a distraction from the ‘Keep the people ignorant and fighting each other, and they won’t notice the plutocrats picking their pockets’ is right there on page one of the oligarch’s playbook.And MAGA falls for this shit, every time — because stupid doesn’t magically cure itself overnight.Now, listen — I’m not saying that folks should prank this new anti-fraud hotline, but I’m not saying they shouldn’t.You see, the government of Missouri had themselves a bright idea: transgendered people aren’t being persecuted enough, so let’s make it easier to single them out for abuse. And so they created a web form where complete fucking busybodies could rat on their neighbors.Pranksters flooded the snitch form with so much hilarious garbage that it had to be shut down.Now, I know what you’re going to say next. “But Uncle Jeff, you’ve already written over eleven hundred words, and you still haven’t told us what we really want to know: at any point during yesterday’s Oval Bordello dog-and-pony show, did Donny melt down at a reporter’s question and throw an infantile shit-fit?”“Listen to you. Hey. Hey! I’m not— You better, you better — I don’t know the hell you are, but you better be careful.”“Wait. Wait. Quiet. QUIET! What’s wrong with you? Are you a sick person? I actually think there’s something wrong with you.”What a fucking child. Tell me again how women don’t have the temperament to be president. That’s such a cool story.Donny actually did it a time, but some idiot forgot to bookmark it last night when he was making notes for this post.Dear Leader held another hate-rally last night, in who the fuck even cares where. The demented old shitbag rambled incoherently for a merciless hour and fifty-four minutes. I’m not even going to bother to write about it. It was virtually identical to all the hate-rallies I’ve been covering for weeks now. Same shit, different day.“So, he’s over here, I’m over here. And— I’m studying his body. I've never studied the body of a man before. It’s not my thing. Nothing wrong with it, of course. Heh heh. Nothing— I always proceed it by saying ‘nothing wrong.’ But it’s never been my thing, to be honest with you. But I looked at his ass. And then I looked at his legs. And I said it might— and I said, ‘his ass is shit.’ It’s like— it’s like a pile of muscle. Then I looked at his legs. And I said, ‘man, his feet are big.’ Then I looked at his shoulders and I tapped him on the shoulder, and it actually hurt my hand. It was like a piece of steel.”You have to e that Donny stuck a ‘not that there’s anything wrong with that’ in there. Congratulations, MAGA. You elected a gay president — and you didn’t even know it.Not that there’s anything wrong with that.And now, it’s time to ourselves out of here. We’ve earned it.Let’s do some more selfies that I downloaded off of Ms Spouse’s phone. This one’s from the hallway, on May 16, 2020.This one’s from the bathroom, also on May 16, 2020.And lastly, from the patio, on August 5, 2021. I love the framing on this one.Have a great Wednesday, everyone.here’s your daily reminder that I can be found on Blue Sky at this link.this is going to be my closing message for the foreseeable future: do what you need to do to keep sane. if that means you need to disengage with my daily posts for a while, I get it. this community of ours will still be here when you return.to all the people who have signed on in the days since the election, . settle in as we all try to deal with the shitfuckery that’s ahead of us.we are all in this together, and we are all here for each other.

item.title: The SpeechRecognition API
item.content:encoded: There’s an older deaf gentleman in my town who’s very friendly, and likes to communicate with rudimentary hand gestures, but I have a hard time understand what he’s trying to say.I’d love to learn American Sign Language (ASL) at some point (shoutout King Ron), but until then, I wanted an app that could convert speech into text.Every transcription app I found required a pretty expensive subscription… so I decided to build my own using web technologies!Press the microphone button to listen to text and display it in the UI in real-time. You can also type/edit text manually with a keyboard.The app works in Chrome, Edge, and Safari, but in Vivaldi or Firefox (more on that later).The web API can take spoken audio and convert it into text.Some browsers use a prefixed implementation, so to start, need to define and variables that account for both the unprefixed and prefixed objects.The creates a new instance. We can then define a handful of properties on it. - If , it converts speech as the user talks. If , it converts in one operation when the user is done (defaults to ). - The language to use. - If , return interim results before the session is done (defaults to ). - The number of possible matches to return per word or phrase.When the user presses the button (or in some other way toggles speech-to-text), run the method to start listening and transcribing.When they press the button again (or in some other way stop listening), run the method.While the instance is running, it will emit events with an iterator of transcription .Each item in contains an iterator of transcriptions (up to the number of provided). Each one has a property with the text.You can convert the array of into a string using the and methods. Here, I’m displaying them as text inside an element in the UI.So… why doesn’t this work in Vivaldi, a Chromium browser, if it works in Chrome and Edge? And why does it work in Safari but not Firefox?The API isn’t a web API. Transcription isn’t built into browsers. The audio is send to a third-party service.Chromium browsers use Google’s API. Safari uses Apple’s.Because Google owns Chrome, they get it for free. Microsoft pays for it in Edge. Vivaldi and Firefox do not, so the “web API” doesn’t work.There is an option for local-only mode, but it doesn’t seem to actually work anywhere.

item.title: Nobody Wants To Talk About Why The Ringer Is Pivoting To Substack
item.author: Owen Lewis
item.content:encoded: A media company launching a series of paywalled newsletters is not, on its own and on its face, a strange thing to do. AI’s ongoing cannibalization of online search is ravaging website traffic, and programmatic advertising doesn’t provide the kind of revenue it used to. If you were running a website like The Ringer, you might decide that it makes financial sense to put writing from some of your most popular staffers behind a paywall. That's exactly what has happened: Sean Fennessey, Zach Lowe, Tom Pelissero, and Bryan Curtis have all recently launched newsletters, only one of which (Curtis’s) is free. This seemingly normal business decision comes with a quirk, though, which is that the newsletters are being published on Substack. Nobody at The Ringer, or Substack, will tell you why.This odd arrangement naturally raises a few questions: Why not just publish these writers’ work on The Ringer’s existing website? Does Spotify, which has owned The Ringer since 2020, somehow not have the technical capability to build its own paywall? If all of this valuable writing is going to live on an entirely different platform, what does that mean for the future of The Ringer’s editorial operation? Have the executives in charge of The Ringer, like seemingly everyone else, surrendered to the idea that Substack is the only place where people will actually read things anymore?I emailed a few questions along these lines to Fennessey, a founder and executive at The Ringer, and more general questions to Lowe, Curtis, and Pelissero. None of them replied. I also reached out to Substack and Spotify, figuring that if the two companies had agreed on some sort of arrangement to produce these newsletters, their respective comms departments would be eager to trumpet their synergistic disruption of the publishing space. Neither company replied. It took reaching out to Ringer editor-in-chief Ben Glicksman to receive something resembling an official response. That came from Mallory Morehead Pritzl, part of the PR team for Spotify: "Thanks for reaching out. We are not commenting at this time."

item.title: Why TV Can't Tell Stories Chronologically
item.author: Miss Cellania
item.content:encoded: The use of the flashback in telling a story has been around forever. In the hands of skilled storyteller, it can be a very effective device. The author wants to control how much the audience knows, and at what point everything can be revealed. However, in modern TV shows, the narrative flashes back and forth so often that the viewer may end up dizzy. These multiple timelines can keep us guessing, or make us just give up. Is this just a trend in the art of storytelling? Or is it a way to pad out a too-short main story and make it last through the planned season? Or is it just fun for the cast and crew? The difference between a flashback as a stunt or an effective storytelling device is how necessary it is to making the story coherent and satisfying to watch or read.

item.title: Trump’s 2020 schemer begs SCOTUS for his law license back
item.author: 1axbx29zudb0kn9mjtnthi58rz8cnayvx3espv@bf56x.hubspotemail.net
item.content:encoded: Remember John Eastman? He was a prominent lawyer for Trump’s 2020 campaign, best known as a key architect of the president’s effort to overturn the results of that election. Eastman drafted a memo arguing that Vice President Mike Pence should throw out the electoral votes for Joe Biden in seven key states. argued that Congress doesn’t actually have a role in certifying federal elections — “all the Members of Congress can do is watch,” he wrote. That effort got Eastman barred from practicing law by the State Bar Court of California. Now he’s asking the Supreme Court to overturn the disbarment.By the way, this isn’t the only recent example of a key election denier fighting “barfare” — a new term cooked up by MAGA to describe far-right lawyers facing consequences for doing things like plotting to overturn an election. Former Trump lawyer Jeffrey Clark — who was also disbarred for his efforts to help Trump steal the 2020 vote — recently launched a law firm aimed at fighting “barfare.”There’s a nonzero chance the Supreme Court might take up Eastman’s case. Last week, it asked the State Bar for a response, which means at least one justice was interested enough in the case to want more information.And Eastman has the support of election deniers, prominent MAGA figures and Republican politicians. Fourteen briefs were filed with SCOTUS supporting his bid.One of the briefs was from 17 current and former Trump-allied lawyers — most of whom were also involved in the president’s scheme to overturn the 2020 election — including anti-voting lawyer Cleta Mitchell, former One America News Network reporter Christina Bobb, former Trump DOJ official Ed Martin, and lawyers Jenna Ellis and Sidney Powell.“That whole proceeding in CA is a travesty and must be reversed,” Mitchell wrote on social media. “SCOTUS should put a stop to this abuse of the bar disciplinary process being used as a partisan political weapon. This is a well funded, leftwing coordinated conspiracy and SCOTUS needs to address it.”Another brief supporting Eastman came from Sens. Ted Cruz (R-Texas) and Mike Lee (R-Utah), who urged the Supreme Court to take the case “because free and independent advocacy is essential to self-government and to a functioning judicial system.”Eastman himself chimed in on the various briefs filed in support of his petition: “Collectively, they tell a powerful story both of the First Amendment violations we’ve raised but also of the broader risk posed by barfare, particularly in intensely partisan election disputes,” Eastman wrote on social media.

In her original music, she foregrounds the piano and adorns the tracks with synth pads/arps and field recordings. “My music is based on three core components I like to call the ‘3 I’s,’ she told 15Questions: “improvisation, intuition, and introspection.” Her new record, El Miedo No es Una Opción is a collaboration with Chilean composer Nico Rosenberg. item.title: The "Lost" Empire Strikes Back Documentary by Michel Parbot
item.author: Miss Cellania
item.content:encoded: In 1980, French filmmaker Michel Parbot made an hour-long TV documentary on the filming of the second movie. The Making of 'The Empire Strikes Back' was lost for many years (although short clips were passed around), but apparently Adywan, a French fan, found a film copy somewhere, and it is now available for the first time in its entirety on YouTube. Enjoy behind-the-scenes footage of fight choreography, an extended look at the struggles of filming on Hoth (Norway), learn how special effects were done before CGI, and hear stories from the professionals involved in the production.

item.title: New Entrant Pollster Was Publishing All Fake Polls
item.author: Josh Marshall
item.source: Josh Marshall – TPM – Talking Points Memo
item.content:encoded: A crazy, crazy story unfolding tonight in the online virtual terrain of political social media and poll-watching. It’s late. But I will give you the bare outline. Seemingly out of the blue earlier this evening an outfit called “Wedgewood Polling” put out a press release stating that all but one of their polls had been fake and that the fakery was all part of a “social experiment” to test how easy it would be to produce fake polls that got aggregated on the big aggregation sites and made their way into news stories. If you’re thinking, wait, didn’t I hear something like this last summer? Yes, you did. There was a smaller-scale version of this, with the same “social experiment” rationale back in August. “Wedgewood,” though, released a lot of polls, in a number of high profile races, not just two or three of them. And there’s at least an argument that they meaningfully impacted some Democratic primary races. They certainly helped shape some campaign narratives. They had appeared to be the only independent poll of the Mississippi Senate race and the only one at all since August.

item.title: Humpday Hottie: Anne Hathaway
item.author: Schill
item.content:encoded: Anne Hathaway is an American actress known for moving comfortably between romantic comedies, dramas, musicals, action films, and prestige productions. Born in Brooklyn, New York, in 1982, she developed an interest in acting at a young age and began her professional career in television before landing the role that made her a star.Hathaway became internationally famous as Mia Thermopolis in Disney’s (2001). Her performance as an awkward teenager who discovers she is heir to a European kingdom made her a major young star almost overnight. She returned for The Princess Diaries 2: Royal Engagement in 2004, further establishing the character as one of her best-known early roles.Rather than remaining associated exclusively with family-oriented films, Hathaway deliberately expanded her range. She appeared in movies including , , and . Her performance as Andy Sachs in became particularly iconic, with the film becoming one of the most enduring fashion-related comedies of the 2000s.Hathaway later demonstrated her abilities in more demanding roles. She won the Academy Award for Best Supporting Actress for playing Fantine in the 2012 musical , delivering a performance that brought her considerable critical recognition. She also appeared as Selina Kyle/Catwoman in Christopher Nolan’s , adding a major action role to her résumé.Her filmography has continued to span very different genres, including science fiction, comedy, drama, and romance. Movies such as , , , and have allowed her to continue moving between mainstream entertainment and more character-driven projects.With a career spanning more than two decades, Hathaway has successfully transitioned from child and young-adult roles into one of Hollywood’s most versatile leading actresses.

item.title: eMudhra Intermediate CA Compromise
item.author: Simon Willison
item.content:encoded: This is very, very bad news:The private keys of eight eMudhra intermediate CA certificates have been compromised. They chain to roots trusted by the Mozilla, Microsoft, Apple and Chrome root programs and by many downstream trust stores.Any software that bundles a list of trusted certificates needs to be updated. This site is tracking software updates via this GitHub repository - Linux distros need to update their packages.
